easy ranch beans
SERVES 6

1 pound dried black
peans, picked over and
rinsed, or 2 15-ounce cans
black beans, rinsed
and drained

1 teaspoon baking soda

4 raw bacon strips,
chopped

1 tablespoon vegetable oil

1 large white onion, finely
chopped

8 scallions, white and light
green parts only, finely
chopped

4 medium tomatoes,
peeled, cored, and
chopped

3 large celery stalks, grated

1 garlic clove, finely minced

1 bay leaf

Y2 teaspoon smoked paprika
powder

¥2 teaspoon ground coriander

Y2 teaspoon salt

The high plains past the county line are about the emptiest
country you will ever drive through. Picture it: flat and windy, with
long gold evenings and a sky that goes on for
a hundred miles. It’s cattle country out there,
and a pot of beans like this one has fed a lot of tired hands.
Set out warm tortillas, a fried €gg, and hot sauce and nobody
leaves the table hungry. When there's no time for the knife work,
pulse the onion, scallions, celery, and garlic
in your food processor until they're fine, then add
the tomatoes and pulse once or twice more.

J dried beans, leave them in cold water overnight with
yon of baking soda. The next morning, drain the beans
in a heavy pot with the bacon, another V2 teaspoon
da, and 6 cups of water. Bring up to a boil, turn the
heat down to a bare simmer, and cook the beans until they are creamy,
about 90 minutes. If the pot starts to look dry before the beans are ten-
der, top it up with a cup of water (or more as needed). If using canned
beans, warm them in a heavy pot with 3%2 cups of water.

Heat the oil in a wide skillet over medium-high heat for
1 minute. Add the rest of the ingredients and cook, stirring
often, until everything is soft and smells sweet, 5 to 7 minutes.

Tip the vegetable mixture into the pot with the beans and simmer
3 just long enough for the pot to come together, about 10 min-
utes. Fish out the bay leaf before serving.

pantry tip: If using canned beans, simply add the
bacon and vegetables once they have softened
